guarantees_lost_or_changed: The unqualified current privileged/all-writer protection claim would become conditional on an explicitly bounded trusted infrastructure.
No promised prevention of deliberate trusted-administrator, kernel/hypervisor or raw device/physical tampering; observation of every such breach is also not guaranteed.
Missing trusted-infrastructure conformance can invalidate the proposed protection claim even if workload checks pass.
Revocation would prevent new declared-operation admission, rather than every internal effect immediately after the external revocation request.
Internal effects of an admitted operation could occur between the request and its known safe cut; no response latency or cut bound is proven here.
This changes original fence/forward semantics and associated observers/oracle expectations; it is not compatible with the current every-effect clause as written.

Time-integrity protection would become conditional on explicitly trusted local host/time infrastructure rather than treating every privileged or hidden clock-domain manipulation as an independently enforceable threat.
No guarantee of detecting deliberate hidden kernel/hypervisor clock manipulation or snapshot rollback by assumed-trusted actors, even when a boot identifier appears unchanged.

A local read or delivered timer alone supplies neither an absolute response/drain bound nor authenticated issuer/time mapping or durable rights. The proposal changes the clock trust claim, not the original finite deadline or recovery budget.

The original stage12 function/name/operation/guard/stream paths and event membership would change to a producer-only stage with separate external finalization; this is not original whole-stage12 conformance.
Producer exit alone would no longer be the original full last-stage status/eligibility; separate receipt/observer/custody results become explicit requirements.

A finite declared terminal acceptance/evidence boundary introduces a scope/trust cut requiring a full migration. Complete native accounting of that boundary is unproved; later unclassified effects cannot be ignored.

proposed_clause_text./guard_contract/admission: Before native entry, independently establish complete in-boundary writer membership, protected object and alias identities, continuous exclusion and approved infrastructure assumptions. Unknown actor membership, uncontrolled in-boundary writer, foreign overlap or unverifiable guard blocks entry. A known infrastructure trust failure latches stop/failure; suspected or unclassifiable breach remains pending. No automatic restoration, relaunch, refund, rebind or reacquisition follows.
proposed_clause_text./guard_contract/coverage: Cover all seven original domains plus source, owned, recovery, evidence and publication objects, ancestors, mounts, backing routes, handles and complete consumers. Require proven coordination or prevention for every actor inside the reviewed workload threat boundary, including direct, manual, scheduled, helper and privileged workload writers. Exclude deliberate tampering by the explicitly enumerated trusted host infrastructure only as a disclosed assumption, never as prevention evidence.
proposed_clause_text.trusted_host_assumption: The specifically identified host kernel/enforcement implementation, policy administrator, hypervisor if present, storage controller/device and physical access custodians follow the reviewed policy and device specification throughout the attempt. Deliberate privileged policy changes or direct out-of-policy backing-object effects by these trusted actors are outside this proposed protection guarantee. Ordinary workload helpers, updater/backends, scheduled/manual tools and external writers are never exempt merely because they run as root.

proposed_clause_text./fence_contract/rule: The external controller serializes original-attempt admission at each enumerated operation cut. Revocation denies every subsequent admission. An operation already admitted may finish only its declared finite effects and descendants before its declared safe cut, inside the original scope, fixed deadline and pre-spent budget. This permits effects after a forward-revocation request but never new operation admission, a renewed deadline or unbounded completion.
proposed_clause_text./forward_contract/in_flight: Each admitted operation requires independently reviewed exact graph/effects/identities/descendants, finite limits, valid original rights and known safe cut. Missing or unknown cut prevents admission; a cut label, backend return or stop request is not known drain. Scoped recovery/evidence/publication keeps its own original rights and is not blanket exempt.
proposed_clause_text./forward_contract/termination: Forward revocation closes new admission irreversibly and requires original admitted operations to reach a declared safe cut. Expiry, original deadline or any failure retains absorbing stop; no effect beyond the original permitted finite scope/deadline is authorized. Unknown stopping or completion remains pending. No new operation, launch, grant, retry, refund or reacquisition follows.

proposed_clause_text./clock_contract/rule: Authenticate the issuer's original fixed finite bounds and map them once at admission to an independently reviewed local elapsed-time clock domain under an explicitly enumerated conforming host kernel/hardware/hypervisor assumption. Preserve the original boot/clock-domain identity, exact mapping, fixed deadlines and durable budget. Suspend elapsed time must be accounted for or further effects denied before resume; missing/unknown mapping, boot drift, observed or suspected discontinuity, snapshot/restore or provider loss blocks effects. No clock fallback, deadline renewal, budget refill or right revival.
proposed_clause_text.local_clock_trust_assumption: Only specifically identified host kernel/time infrastructure, hardware and hypervisor behavior following the reviewed policy/specification are trusted for elapsed-time integrity. Deliberate hidden clock-domain manipulation or snapshot rollback by those assumed-trusted actors is outside this proposed integrity guarantee. It is not guaranteed detectable; observed/suspected violations invalidate admission. Ordinary suspend, restart, scheduler delay and timer loss remain in-scope reviewed failures. No actual provider or clock ID is selected.

proposed_clause_text.external_finalization_obligation: After complete producer subject trace closure, bind a non-secret receipt payload from captured closed data only. Receipt records prior subject streams/status/origin and artifact identity/evidence, never its own future completion. Commit the separate receipt once under original finite publication rights; independently observe exact final object/storage and all receipt-writer outcomes. Consumer custody/ACK and every collector/observer effect require separate known independent accounting before overall eligibility. No same-payload proof of own final completion, no atomic archive/sidecar pair and no replay on uncertainty.
proposed_clause_text.terminal_acceptance_cut: The proposed finite evidence boundary ends only after every enumerated subject/receipt/collector/observer/consumer outcome is independently known under reviewed finite controls. No further evidence-producing effect is included after that declared cut; any real later effect is an unclassified obligation and blocks closure. No infinite self-receipt chain is required or claimed solved. A designated external custody/acceptance boundary has explicit source/trust/storage/clock/rights responsibilities; its complete native closure and trust are unknown, not exempt or assumed established.

new_joint_wording.text: One explicit proposed infrastructure trust boundary applies consistently to source, writer, clock, storage and terminal custody control assumptions. Enumerate kernel/enforcement and time providers, policy administrator, hypervisor if present, storage hardware and physical custodians by exact identity/configuration before any future acceptance. Their deliberate policy/device/time tampering is outside the proposed guarantee and is not promised detectable. Ordinary direct/manual/scheduled/privileged workload, updater, helpers, backend, observers and injectors remain in scope. Conforming-infrastructure assumptions never prove actual isolation, correct storage or independent custody. All actual identities and support remain unknown.

Use an externally controlled draft operation-admission boundary with the original worker bootstrap and no inherited worker broker/service/validation channel. Forward revocation irreversibly denies subsequent forward admission. An already admitted operation may continue only its explicitly enumerated finite effects and descendants toward its independently known safe cut within its original scope, fixed deadline and pre-spent budget. Effects after a revocation request are an intentional changed promise. Expiry/failure or reaching the fixed bound creates no permission beyond that bound. Each original recovery/evidence/publication scope needs its separate valid rights and explicit revocation treatment. The original every-effect forward-validity and recovery-validity clauses still need complete exact replacement or retained per-scope enforcement reconciliation at402; no joint enforcement protocol is supplied here.

Combine a hypothetical protected guardian with the proposed enumerated local-time infrastructure assumption. Guardian membership and all descendants, inherited handles, streams and in-flight effects must be established before effects. The issuer original fixed finite bounds are mapped once to the reviewed original boot/clock domain; suspend consumes elapsed bounds or effects are denied before resume. Guardian control requests or survival are not known drain. Guardian/clock loss, uncertainty, restart, observed/suspected discontinuity or unknown stopping blocks dependent effects and preserves scoped pending obligations. No immortal guardian, guaranteed finite drain, clock fallback, deadline renewal, recovery exemption, new grant or replay is introduced. Hidden deliberate time tampering by the enumerated trusted infrastructure is outside the proposed integrity guarantee; detection is not promised. Known drain/restoration/release requirements are retained; compatible actual mechanisms remain unresolved.
